blocks.html_cs: Připojování řetězců na konec existujícího řetězce je snadné pomocí operátoru +=, append() nebo push_back().

blocks.html:
string& string::operator+= (const string& str)
string& string::append (const string& str)

  • Both functions append the characters of str to the string.
  • Both functions return *this so they can be “chained”.
  • Both functions throw a length_error exception if the result exceeds the maximum number of characters.

Sample code:

std::string sString{"one"};

sString += std::string{" two"};

std::string sThree{" three"};
sString.append(sThree);

std::cout << sString << '\n';

Output:

one two three

string& string::append (const string& str, size_type index, size_type num)

  • This function appends num characters from str, starting at index, to the string.
  • Returns *this so it can be “chained”.
  • Throws an out_of_range if index is out of bounds
  • Throws a length_error exception if the result exceeds the maximum number of characters.

Sample code:

std::string sString{"one "};

const std::string sTemp{"twothreefour"};
sString.append(sTemp, 3, 5); // append substring of sTemp starting at index 3 of length 5
std::cout << sString << '\n';

Output:

one three

string& string::append (const char* str, size_type len)

  • Appends the first len characters of str to the string.
  • Returns *this so they can be “chained”.
  • Throw a length_error exception if the result exceeds the maximum number of characters.
  • Ignores special characters (including ”)

Sample code:

std::string sString{"one "};

sString.append("threefour", 5);
std::cout << sString << '\n';

Output:

one three

This function is dangerous and its use is not recommended.

blocks.html: Now you might be wondering why the name of the function is push_back() and not append(). This follows a naming convention used for stacks, where push_back() is the function that adds a single item to the end of the stack. If you envision a string as a stack of characters, using push_back() to add a single character to the end makes sense. However, the lack of an append() function is inconsistent in my view!
blocks.preview: Now you might be wondering why the name of the function is push_back() and not a
blocks.html_cs: Nyní vás možná zajímá, proč je název funkce push_back() a ne append(). Toto se řídí konvencí pojmenování používanou pro zásobníky, kde push_back() je funkce, která přidá jednu položku na konec zásobníku. Pokud si představujete řetězec jako hromadu znaků, použití push_back() k přidání jednoho znaku na konec dává smysl. Absence funkce append() je však podle mého názoru nekonzistentní!

string& string::append (size_type num, char c)

  • Adds num occurrences of the character c to the string
  • Returns *this so it can be “chained”.
  • Throws a length_error exception if the result exceeds the maximum number of characters.

Sample code:

std::string sString{"aaa"};

sString.append(4, 'b');
std::cout << sString << '\n';

Output:

aaabbbb
